S204: Application of Bylaw The application of this bylaw is subject to 24 VSA, Chapter 117. Except as hereinafter provided, no building or structure shall be erected, moved, altered or extended, and no land excavated or structure, or land part thereof shall be occupied or used unless in conformity with this bylaw as herein specified for the district in which such structure is located. Any use not permitted by this bylaw shall be deemed prohibited. paragraphs: S302: Existing Small Lots Any lot in individual and separate and non-affiliated ownership from surrounding properties in existence on the effective date of this bylaw may be developed for the purposes permitted in the district in which it is located, even though not conforming to minimum lot size requirements, if such lot is not less than one-eighth acre in area with a minimum width or depth dimension of forty feet. S303: Frontage or, or Access to Public Roads or Waters No land development may be permitted on lots which do not either have frontage on a public road or public waters or, with the site plan approval of the Planning Commission, access to such a road or waters by a permanent casement or right-of-way at least twenty feet in width. [24 VSA, S4412(3)] Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 15 S304: Protection of Home Occupations

sections.title: No regulation herein is intended to infringe upon the right of any resident to use a
paragraphs: portion of a dwelling for an occupation which is customary in residential areas and which does not change the character thereof. [24 VSA, S4412(4)]

sections.title: Exterior displays or signs other than those normally permitted in the district, exterior
paragraphs: storage of materials, and exterior indication of the home occupation or variation from the residential character of the principal structure shall not be permitted. S305: Family Childcare Homes A family child care home serving six or fewer children shall be considered to constitute a permitted use of a single-unit dwelling. S306: Residential Care and Group Homes A residential care home or group home, to be operated under state licensing or registration, serving not more than eight persons who have a handicap or disability as defined in 9 V.S.A. S4501, shall be considered to constitute a permitted use of a single-unit dwelling. S307: Calculation of Required Lot Area When creating one or more lots, such lots shall be of sufficient area and dimensions to comply with the minimum lot area and dimensional requirements set forth in this bylaw for the district in which such lots are proposed. Existing or proposed rights-of-way or public sites shall not be included as part of a lot for the purpose of compliance with the minimum area and dimensional requirements. S308: Lots in Two Zoning Districts Where a district boundary line divides a lot of record at the time such line is adopted, the regulations for the less restricted part of such lot shall extend not more than thirty feet into the more restricted part, provided the lot has frontage on a street in the less restricted district. S309: Principal Uses on Lots There shall be only one principal use on a lot unless otherwise permitted by S205. S310: Reduction of Lot Area No lot shall be so reduced in area such that the area, yards, lot width, frontage, coverage or other requirements of this bylaw shall be smaller than herein prescribed for each district. No lot shall be made smaller than is prescribed for each district. S311: Required Area or Yards Space required under this bylaw to satisfy area, yard, or other open space requirements in Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 16 relation to one principal use or structure shall not be counted as part of a required open space for any other principal use or structure. S312: Yards on Corner Lots Any yard adjoining a street shall be considered a front yard for the purposes of this bylaw. However, only one front yard is required to comply with the minimum depth requirement. All other front yards shall either equal the front yard minimum or shall be at least twenty-five feet in depth. S313: Projections into Required Yards All structures, whether attached to the principle structure or not, and whether open or enclosed, including porches, carports, balconies, or platforms above normal grade level, shall not project into any minimum required front, side, or rear yard. S314: Temporary Uses and Structures Temporary permits may be issued by the Zoning Administrator for a period not exceeding one year, for non-conforming uses or structures incidental to construction projects located on the same lot, provided such permits are conditioned upon agreement by the applicant to remove the structure or use upon expiration of the permit. Such permits may not be renewed. S315: Excavation With the exception of rock cuts, no grading, cutting, or filling shall be carried out in any district which leaves the slope of the existing grade in excess of one foot measured vertically for every two feet measured horizontally unless an approved vegetative ground cover or other soil stabilization technique is used. Stabilized slopes shall have a maximum grade of 1 foot measured vertically for every foot measured horizontally. This section shall pertain only to excavations in excess of 1,000 square feet in area. S316: Obstruction of Vision In all districts on a corner lot, within the triangular area formed by the intersection of two street property lines and a third line joining them at points twenty-five feet away from their intersection, there shall be no obstruction to vision between the height of two feet and twelve feet above the average grade of each street. S317: Height Exceptions and Restrictions Except within 3,000 feet of an aircraft landing strip, nothing herein contained shall be interpreted to limit or restrict the height of silos, church spires, cupolas, and bell and clock towers and essential public utility structures. S318: Signs Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 17 The purpose of this section is to promote and protect the public health, safety, and welfare by regulating existing and proposed signs in the Town of Groton. It is further intended to hereby protect the economic and scenic value of the Town, and in order to prevent hazards to users of roads in the Town.

paragraphs: lies within four hundred feet of an entrance to the principle building. Such parking configuration shall be approved by the Board of Adjustment for a use that requires Conditional Use approval. All other uses shall be approved by the Planning Commission in Site Plan Review.

S323: Off-Street Loading and Unloading Space Requirements For every building hereafter erected, altered, extended or changed in use for the purpose of business, trade, or industry there shall be provided ample space that is not restrictive of traffic:

sections.title: Hotels, Motels, Commercial, Business, Service and Industrial Establishments: one
paragraphs: loading and unloading space for every 10,000 square feet of floor area or fraction thereof.

sections.title: Wholesale, Warehouse, Freight and Trucking Uses: one off-street loading space for
paragraphs: every 7,500 square feet of floor area or fraction thereof. S324: Travel Trailers It shall be unlawful for any person to park a camping trailer, travel trailer, pick-up coach, or motor home on any public or private property, except in accordance with the regulations below:

sections.title: In an approved travel trailer park
In an approved sales, service, storage and repair facility
A person may park or store his/her travel trailer on his/her property without a permit
paragraphs: providing it is no closer than six feet to any property line and as long as it is not occupied for more than six (6) months in a calendar year.

sections.title: No travel trailer or recreational vehicle shall be occupied for longer than six (6) months
paragraphs: in any calendar year nor permanently located on a lot unless such lot and travel trailer or recreational vehicle complies with the minimum lot area and dimensional requirements for the district in which the travel trailer or recreational vehicle is or is to be located. Such travel trailer or recreational vehicle shall also comply with all other requirements, including permitting, found herein that are applicable to single family Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 21 dwellings. S325: Sewage Regulation Please see: Environmental Protection Rules, Chapter 1, Wastewater System and Potable Water Supply Rules, Effective Sept. 29, 2007 or the latest version as promulgated by the State of Vermont. . S326: Screened Service Area Requirements In any district, any area designated, used or intended to be used as a service area for any building or land use, other than one family and two family dwellings, shall be screened from view with either a wall, a solid fence or a hedge of evergreens at a height of at least five feet above grade level on all sides where the adjacent land is in a residential district or residential use. S327: Burned Buildings No owner or occupant of land in any district shall permit fire or other ruins to be left, but within eighteen (18) months shall remove or refill the same to clear ground level or shall repair, rebuild or replace the structure. This provision shall not apply when a burned structure is the subject of an arson trial and the burned structure must be maintained for evidentiary purposes. S328: Planned Unit Development With the approval of a site plan the Planning Commission is hereby empowered to vary certain zoning regulations under the criteria and procedures established in 24 VSA, S4417).

sections.title: Proposals for planned unit development shall be submitted to the Planning
paragraphs: Commission. The material accompanying the proposal shall contain the following: Required site plan shall depict all buildings, parking areas, and landscaping at a scale sufficient to pen-nit the study of all elements of the plan. All utilities shall also be shown and described. Typical elevations and floor plans may also be required. In addition, the site plans shall show the adjacent building outlines and other outstanding features within 200 feet of the proposed Planned Unit Development. Any change in grading shall be shown.

subsections.title: An environment in harmony with surrounding development

paragraphs: the district in which the plan is located. In a planned unit development, development in a residential district, commercial, educational and public facilities may be allowed which are designed to serve the development and the area around the development.

sections.title: Lot size, width, front yard depth, and side yard requirements may be waived; however,
paragraphs: these will be evaluated by the Planning Commission on their individual merit.

sections.title: A planned unit development shall comply with the following standards:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Shall be at least ten contiguous acres except in the Conservation District, which shall
paragraphs: be at least 50 contiguous acres.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: The developer of a planned unit development with 6 or more units may be required to
paragraphs: install common water and/or sewer systems to serve such development.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Adequate space shall be left open for common usage. This may be waived by the
paragraphs: Planning Commission for commercial and industrial planned unit developments providing adequate screening and landscaping is provided.

sections.title: The Planning Commission may prescribe, from time to time, rules and regulations to
paragraphs: supplement the standards and conditions set forth in this zoning bylaw for planned unit development, provided the rules and regulations are not inconsistent with the zoning bylaw. The Planning Commission shall hold a public hearing after public notice as required by 24 VSA, S4464(a), prior to the establishment of any supplementary rules and regulations for planned unit development. S329: Campgrounds

sections.title: Permit Required. It shall be unlawful for any person to construct, maintain or operate
paragraphs: any campground within the limits of the Town of Groton unless the owner and operator hold a valid permit. Upon approval of the Planning Commission, the Zoning Administrator shall issue a permit, which shall be contingent upon compliance with this local regulation.

sections.title: Permit-Method of Application and Requirements. Applications for permits shall be
paragraphs: made in writing, signed by the applicant who shall file with the application proof of ownership of the premises or of a lease or written permission from the owner thereof together with a complete set of plans drawn to scale, showing the location of the proposed campground and which shall include:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: The areas and dimension of the tract of land

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: The maximum number, location and size of all camping spaces

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: The location of any existing buildings, roadways, parking areas, walkways and
paragraphs: Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 23 turn outs.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: The location of electrical, water, storm drainage and sewer lines and sewage
paragraphs: disposal systems.

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: A contour map showing the proposed grading of the campground

sections.title: Construction or Enlargement of Campgrounds. No person shall construct or enlarge a
paragraphs: campground without first obtaining approval from the Planning Commission and conditional use approval from the Board of Adjustment, if required. Before such a permit may be issued, there must be favorable recommendation by a majority of the Planning Commission. Before granting approval, the Planning Commission may require a performance bond from the operator of the campground to assure that the campground is constructed and maintained in a satisfactory manner. The Planning Commission, in the interest of public safety, health and welfare, may require and other improvements and facilities before approving the campground. The Planning Commission may accept the proposed plan, accept the proposed plan with recommended changes or reject the plan. The Commission shall submit the application and the plan to the Zoning Administrator, together with the Commission's action regarding the permit.

sections.title: Campground Standards. The following regulations shall apply in respect to all
paragraphs: campgrounds.

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Campground shall have an area of no less than 10 acres

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Campgrounds shall provide for individual trailer spaces, access driveways and
paragraphs: parking.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Each campsite shall be at least 2,500 square feet in area and at least thirty feet in
paragraphs: width and have a compacted gravel surface at least ten feet in width and forty-two feet in length.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: A strip of land at least twenty-five feet in width shall be maintained as a
paragraphs: landscaped area abutting all campground property lines except when the campground boundary is adjacent to residential uses, then the landscaped area shall be at least fifty feet in width. S330: Salvage Yards In all districts, salvage yards shall not be permitted unless permitted by the State of Vermont. S331: Yard Minimums from Private Rights-of-Way When an individual's property abuts a private right-of-way not owned by said individual, any and all structures erected on said individual's property shall be located from the private right-of-way in conformance with the applicable yard minimum. If the property also abuts a public right-of- way, the front yard minimum shall be from such public right-of-way. If the property abuts only a private right-of-way, then the front yard minimum shall be from the private right-of-way. S332: Connection of Driveways, Private Roads, and Curb Cuts Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 24

sections.title: In accordance with 19 VSA, S1111 any driveway or private road connecting to a public
paragraphs: road shall require a driveway permit, whether the driveway or road is intended for permanent or temporary use. When such drive or road is associated with other new construction or change of use, application for the permit may be made concurrently using the Groton Zoning Permit Application form. This form must be used even when no other construction is involved.

sections.title: This application must include a sketch or attached map clearly showing the location of
paragraphs: the access point and distances to the nearest driveways and intersections. In the case of technically difficult, potentially unsafe, or anticipated high-usage connections, the Town may require professionally engineered designs or impose requirements in addition to those specified herein. Guidance for making any connection shall be based on the most recent Vermont Agency of Transportation Standards.

sections.title: Typically only one access point shall be permitted for a single property
Any connection of a driveway, private road, or other curb cut shall be made using a
paragraphs: culvert. When in question the Zoning Administrator may require the applicant to obtain the Road Commissioner's approval of the size and location of the culvert to be installed, or waiver of this requirement.

sections.title: All driveways and private roadways shall be constructed so as not to impair drainage
paragraphs: within the right-of-way, alter the stability of the improved area, or change the drainage of adjacent areas. In no case shall drainage from any driveway or private road run onto the public road. The gradient of the driveway or road shall not exceed 10-percent as it approaches the point of connection. The preferred angle of approach for the intersection of a driveway and a public road is 90-degrees. However, in no case shall the angle of approach be less than 60-degrees.

sections.title: Driveways and private roadways for lots to be newly developed should be constructed
paragraphs: no closer than 20-feet from a property line and no closer than 100-feet from another intersecting street.

sections.title: Shall not be moved, enlarged, or extended
Shall not be changed to another non-conforming use without approval of the Zoning
paragraphs: Board of Adjustment and then only to a use, which, in the opinion of the Zoning Board of Adjustment is of the same, or of a more restricted nature.

sections.title: Shall not be re-established if such use has been discontinued for any reason for a period
paragraphs: of two years, or has been changed to, or replaced by, a conforming use. Intent to resume a nonconforming use shall not confer the right to do so. S403: Non-conforming Buildings The following provisions shall apply to all structures existing on the effective date of this bylaw which do not comply with the lot area, yard minimums and other requirements set forth in this bylaw and all structures which in the future do not comply by reason of any subsequent amendment to this bylaw, or as the result of error by the Zoning Administrator. All non-conforming structures may be continued indefinitely and shall comply with the following:

sections.title: Shall not be moved unless such action conforms to any and all applicable requirements
paragraphs: of this bylaw.

sections.title: May be enlarged or extended providing such enlargement or extension is in
paragraphs: conformance with the requirements of this bylaw and such enlargement or extension does not increase the original structure's degree of non-conformance.

sections.title: Shall not be replaced on the original foundation after such structure has been
paragraphs: voluntarily razed.

sections.title: Shall not be replaced on the original foundation after such structure has been razed due
paragraphs: to fire or other natural damage unless done so within one year following the date of such damage.

sections.title: May receive normal maintenance and repair provided that such action does not increase
paragraphs: the degree of non-conformance.

sections.title: The Zoning Administrator shall be appointed to administer the zoning bylaw pursuant
paragraphs: to 24 VSA, S4448. Said Zoning Administrator shall literally enforce the provisions of this bylaw and in so doing shall inspect developments, maintain records and perform all other necessary tasks to carry out the provisions of this bylaw.

sections.title: An acting Zoning Administrator may be appointed pursuant to 24 VSA, S4448(b)
An interested person may appeal any decision or act taken by the Zoning Administrator
paragraphs: in accordance with S610 of this bylaw. . An interested person means any one of the following:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: A person owning title to property, or a municipality or solid waste management
paragraphs: district empowered to condemn it or an interest in it, affected by a bylaw, who alleges that the bylaw imposes on the property unreasonable or inappropriate restrictions of present or potential use under the particular circumstances of the case.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: The Town of Groton or any adjoining municipality

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: A person owning or occupying property in the immediate neighborhood of a
paragraphs: property that is the subject of any decision or act taken under this chapter, who can demonstrate a physical or environmental impact on the person's interest under the criteria reviewed, and who alleges that the decision or act, if confirmed, will not be in accord with the policies, purposes, or terms of the plan or bylaw of that municipality.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Any ten persons who may be any combination of voters or real property owners in
paragraphs: the Town of Groton who, by signed petition to the Zoning Board Adjustment, allege that any relief requested by a person under this title, if granted, will not be in accord with the policies, purposes, or terms of the plan or bylaw of the Town of Groton. Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 34 This petition to the appropriate municipal panel must designate one person to serve as the representative of the petitioners regarding all matters related to the appeal.

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Any department and administrative subdivision of this state owning property or any
paragraphs: interest in property within the Town of Groton, and the agency of commerce and community development of this state. S602: Zoning Permits

sections.title: No land development, as defined in 24 VSA, S4303(10), may be commenced without a
paragraphs: permit therefore issued by the Zoning Administrator. No zoning permit may be issued by the Zoning Administrator except in conformance with this bylaw.

sections.title: Applications for zoning permits shall be made to the Zoning Administrator on forms
paragraphs: provided by him for that purpose.

sections.title: Prior to the issuance of any zoning permit the Zoning Administrator shall first satisfy
paragraphs: himself that the subject of the application is in conformance with this bylaw. He may request from an applicant any information he deems necessary for this purpose. No such permit shall be issued unless an application, fee, plot plan and any other approvals of the Planning Commission or the Board of Adjustment required by this bylaw have been properly obtained and are submitted in connection with the application. The Zoning Administrator shall, within 30 days of submission of the application, data and approvals, either issue or deny a zoning permit, or refer the permit to the Planning Commission or Zoning Board of Adjustment. If denied, the Zoning Administrator shall so notify the applicant in writing, stating his reasons therefore. If the Zoning Administrator fails to act with regard to a complete application within thirty (30) days, the permit shall be deemed issued on the 31st day. If the zoning permit is approved, all activities authorized by its issuance shall be completed within two years of its date of issue, or the zoning permit shall become null and void and reapplication to complete any activities shall be required.

sections.title: In the issuance of zoning permits, the Zoning Administrator shall comply with all of the
paragraphs: provisions of 24 VSA, S4449.

sections.title: The Board of Selectmen shall establish the fee for a zoning permit. It may be a sliding
paragraphs: scale depending upon the cost of the land development. Said fee shall accompany each application for a permit.

sections.title: No zoning permit issued pursuant to 24 VSA, S4449 shall take effect until the time for
paragraphs: appeal (15 days) in 24 VSA, S4464(a) has passed. In the event that a notice of appeal is properly filed, such permit shall not take effect until the final adjudication of said appeal.

sections.title: The permit shall contain a statement of the period of time within an appeal may be
paragraphs: taken. The permit shall be posted by the applicant within view from the public right-of- way most nearly adjacent to the subject property until the time for appeal has passed.

sections.title: Within three days following the issuance of a permit, the Zoning Administrator shall:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Deliver a copy of the permit to the listers of the municipality; and

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Post a copy of the permit in at least one public place in the municipality until the
paragraphs: expiration of 15 days from the date of issuance of the permit. sections.title: No zoning permit shall be required for the following:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Accepted agricultural or farming practices, including the construction of farm
paragraphs: structures, as such practices are defined by the Commissioner of Agriculture, Food and Markets under 10 V.S.A. S1021 (f). However, any landowner proposing to erect a farm structure shall notify the Zoning Administrator of such intent prior to the erection of such structure. Farm structures shall comply with setbacks approved by the Commissioner of Agriculture, Food and Markets.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Accepted management practices for (silviculture) forestry, as these practices are
paragraphs: defined by the Commissioner of Forests, Parks and Recreation under 6 V.S.A. S4810.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Power generation and transmission facilities, which are regulated under 30 V.S.A
paragraphs: S248 by the Vermont Public Service Board.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Hunting, fishing, and trapping as specified under 24 V.S.A S2295 on private or
paragraphs: public land. This does not include facilities supporting such activities, such as firing ranges or rod and gun clubs, which for the purposes of these regulations are defined as recreation facilities.

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Wind turbines with blades less than 20 feet in diameter, or rooftop solar collectors
paragraphs: less than 10 feet high, any of which are mounted on complying structures.

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: Exterior steps, stairs, landings less than 25 square feet in area, bulkheads, and
paragraphs: handicapped access ramps.

subsections.label: G
subsections.title: Generators, e.g. trailer mounted or on concrete slabs
paragraphs: S604: Limitations The following uses may be regulated only with respect to location, size, height, building bulk, yards, courts, yard minimums, density of buildings, off-street parking, loading facilities, traffic, noise, lighting, landscaping, and screening requirements, and only to the extent that regulations do not have the effect of interfering with the intended functional use:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: State- or community-owned and operated institutions and facilities

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Public and private schools and other educational institutions certified by the state
paragraphs: department of education.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Churches and other places of worship, convents, and parish houses

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Public and private hospitals

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Regional solid waste management facilities certified under 10 V.S.A. Chapter 159

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: Hazardous waste management facilities for which a notice of intent to construct has been
paragraphs: received under 10 V.S.A. 6606a. S605: Penalties Any violation of this bylaw after the effective date thereof shall be punished as provided in 24 VSA, SS4451 and 4452. S606: Planning Commission

sections.title: The Planning Commission shall consist of not less than (3) nor more than nine (9)
paragraphs: members, who shall serve in accordance with 24 V.S.A. S4323(c). Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 37

sections.title: The Planning Commission shall adopt rules of procedure and rules of ethics with
paragraphs: respect to conflicts of interest to guide its official conduct, as required under 24 V.S.A. S4461(a)] and Vermont's Open Meeting Law. The Commission shall have all powers and duties as set forth in the Act to administer the provisions of these regulations, including but not limited to the power to hear and act upon:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Access to non-frontage lots (S303)

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Off-site Parking (S322.01)

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Planned Unit Developments (S328)

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Campground (S329)
paragraphs: S607: Board of Adjustment

sections.title: The Board of Selectmen shall appoint a Board of Adjustment and shall serve for
paragraphs: specified terms in accordance with 24 V.S.A. S4460(b) and (c).

sections.title: The Board of Adjustment shall adopt rules of procedure and rules of ethics with respect
paragraphs: to conflicts of interest to guide its official conduct, as required under 24 V.S.A. S4461(a) and Vermont's Open Meeting Law. The Board of Adjustment shall have all powers and duties as set forth in the Act to administer the provisions of these regulations, including but not limited to power to hear and act upon:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Applications for Conditional Use Approval (S208)

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Appeals of decisions of the Zoning Administrator (S610.01)

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Request for variances (S611)
paragraphs: S608: Public Notice Any public notice required by either this bylaw or 24 VSA, Chapter 117, for any meeting of either the Board of Adjustment or the Planning Commission, shall be given not less than 15 days prior to the date of the public hearing. Public notice shall include the date, time, place, and purpose of such hearing and shall be issued accordingly:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: By the publication in a newspaper of general circulation in Groton

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: By posting in three or more public places within the municipality including posting
paragraphs: within view from the nearest public right of way most nearly adjacent to the property for which an application is made.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: By written notification to the applicant and to owners of all properties adjoining the
paragraphs: property subject to development, without regard to public rights-of-way. This written notice shall include a description of the proposed project, clearly identify how and where additional information may be obtained, and state that participation in the local proceeding is a prerequisite to the right to take any subsequent appeal. S609: Decisions

sections.title: In accordance with 24 V.S.A. S4464(b), the Planning Commission and the Board of
paragraphs: Adjustment shall issue all decisions within 45 days after the adjournment of the hearing. Failure to issue a decision within the 45-day period shall be deemed approval and shall be effective the 46th day.

sections.title: All decisions shall be issued in writing and shall separately state findings of fact and
paragraphs: conclusions of law. Findings of fact shall explicitly and concisely restate the underlying Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 38 facts that support the decision, based exclusively on evidence of the record. Conclusions shall be based on the findings of fact. The decision shall also include a statement of the time within which appeals may be taken. The minutes of a meeting may suffice, provided that the factual basis and conclusions relating to the review standards are provided in accordance with these requirements. 609.03All decisions shall be sent by certified mail, within the required 45-day period, to the applicant or the appellant on matters of appeal. Copies of the decision also shall be mailed to every person appearing and having been heard at the hearing, and filed with the Zoning Administrator and Clerk as part of the public record of the municipality. S610: Appeals of Decisions or Acts of the Zoning Administrator

sections.title: Any interested person may appeal a decision or act of the Zoning Administrator within
paragraphs: 15 days of the date of the decision or act by filing a notice of appeal with the Secretary of the Zoning Board of Adjustment, or the Municipal Clerk if no Secretary has been elected, and by filing a copy of the notice with the Zoning Administrator.

sections.title: The Zoning Board of Adjustment shall hold a public hearing on a notice of appeal
paragraphs: within 60 days of its filing, as required under 24 V.S.A. S4468. The Zoning Board of Adjustment shall give public notice of the hearing in accordance with S608 of this bylaw and mail a copy of the hearing notice to the appellant not less than 15 days prior to the hearing date.

sections.title: The Zoning Board of Adjustment may reject an appeal or request for reconsideration
paragraphs: without hearing, and render a decision which shall include findings of fact within 10 days of the filing of a notice of appeal, if the Zoning Board of Adjustment determines that the issues raised by the appellant have been decided in an earlier appeal or are based on substantially or materially the same facts by or on behalf of the appellant.

sections.title: All decisions of an appeal shall be issued in accordance with S609 of this bylaw
paragraphs: 611: Appeals to Environmental Court

sections.title: An interested person who has participated in a hearing of the Planning Commission or
paragraphs: the Board of Adjustment may appeal any decision or act taken by the either the Planning Commission or the Zoning Board of Adjustment. Such appeal shall be made as provided for in 24 VSA, S4471 to the Environmental Court.

sections.title: Participation in a hearing of the Planning Commission or Board of Adjustment shall
paragraphs: consist of offering, through oral or written testimony, evidence of a statement of concern related to the subject of the hearing. S612: Variances The Board of Adjustment shall hear and decide requests for variances in accordance with 24 V.S.A. S4469(a) and appeal procedures under S610 of these regulations. In granting a variance, the Board of Adjustment may impose conditions it deems necessary and appropriate under the circumstances to implement the purposes of these regulations and the municipal plan currently in effect. The Board of Adjustment may grant a variance and render a decision in favor of the appellant only if all of the following facts are found, and the findings are specified in its written decision:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: There are unique physical circumstances or conditions, including irregularity,
paragraphs: narrowness, or shallowness of lot size or shape, or exceptional topographical or other Town of Groton Zoning Bylaw: Amended 11.15.12 Page 39 physical conditions peculiar to the particular property, and that unnecessary hardship is due to these conditions and not the circumstances or conditions generally created by the provisions of these regulations in the neighborhood or district in which the property is located;

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Because of these physical circumstances or conditions, there is no possibility that the
paragraphs: property can be developed in strict conformity with the provisions of these regulations and that the authorization of a variance is necessary to enable the reasonable use of the property;

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: The unnecessary hardship has not been created by the appellant;

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: The variance, if authorized, will not alter the essential character of the neighborhood or
paragraphs: district in which the property is located, substantially or permanently impair the appropriate use or development of adjacent property, reduce access to renewable energy resources, or be detrimental to the public welfare; and

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: The variance, if authorized, will represent the minimum that will afford relief and will
paragraphs: represent the least deviation possible from these regulations and from the plan.

sections.title: In their interpretation and application, the provisions of this bylaw shall be held to be
paragraphs: minimum requirements adopted for the promotion of the public health, safety, comfort, convenience, and general welfare.

sections.title: Except for 24 VSA, S4413 and where, in this bylaw specifically provided to the
paragraphs: contrary, it is not the intention of this bylaw to repeal, annul, or in any way to impair any regulations or permits previously adopted or issued. However, where this bylaw imposes a greater restriction upon the use of a structure or land than is required by any other statute, ordinance, rule, regulation, permit, easement, or agreement, the provisions of this bylaw shall control. S703: Effective Date This bylaw shall take effect in accordance with the voting and other procedures contained in 21 VSA, S4442. S704: Separability The invalidity of any article or section of this bylaw shall not invalidate any other article or section thereof.
